deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It continues Riemann's reading notes, begun on the previous page (54r), on Theodor Waitz's article 'Die realistische und naturwissenschaftliche Psychologie' (Allgemeine Monatsschrift für Wissenschaft und Literatur, August 1853, p. 655ff.).

The notes close the summary of F. E. Beneke's 'naturwissenschaftliche Psychologie'. Beneke starts from four basic processes of psychic development. The previous page lists the first two:
(1) the formation of new 'Urvermögen' (primitive faculties) in response to external stimuli;
(2) the continual regeneration of the Urvermögen. The continuation 'der Urvermögen' opens this page.
This page then lists the other two:
(3) the constant striving toward equalization of the elements that have become mobile ('das stete Streben nach Ausgleichung der beweglich gewordenen Elemente');
(4) the attraction of the like ('die Anziehung des Gleichartigen').

Riemann then notes that from these Beneke concludes that the soul is an immaterial being (Lehrbuch §§ 20-38).

Bibliographic references follow:
- Beneke, 'Die neue Psychologie. Erläuternde Aufsätze', Berlin 1845.
- 'Lehrbuch der Psychologie als Naturwissenschaft', 2nd edition, 1845. A reference '§ 17 u. 298 Anm.' is struck through.
- 'Pragmatische Psychologie oder Seelenlehre in der Anwendung auf das Leben', 2 vols., Berlin 1850.

The page serves Riemann's philosophical and psychological studies (Herbart, Drobisch, Beneke) underlying his Naturphilosophie fragments. There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Excerpt and summary of Beneke's four basic psychic processes and his inference to the immateriality of the soul, with bibliography (via Waitz 1853)
results.modern_name: History of 19th-century associationist/empirical psychology (Beneke's 'Psychologie als Naturwissenschaft')
results.usually_credited_to: F. E. Beneke (1833/1845); summarized by Th. Waitz (1853)

deep.surprise_reason: These are purely bibliographic reading notes on Beneke's psychology, taken from Waitz's review article. Riemann's interest in Herbartian and contemporary psychology is well known from his published Naturphilosophie fragments. There is no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 'der Urvermögen[?]' is the continuation of item 2 from the previous page ('die fortwährende Regeneration der Urvermögen'); the reading 'Urvermögen' fits the image and context, so the [?] can likely be dropped.
'2te' in '2te Auflage' is underlined in the original.
The struck-through text reads '§ 17 u. 298 Anm.', as the transcription has it.

Full titles for reference: 'Die neue Psychologie. Erläuternde Aufsätze zur zweiten Auflage meines Lehrbuchs der Psychologie als Naturwissenschaft' (Berlin 1845); 'Pragmatische Psychologie oder Seelenlehre in der Anwendung auf das Leben' (2 Bde., Berlin 1850). Riemann's abbreviations 'Ps.' stand for 'Psychologie'.
